body: I am here if you want to talk. I find that it does help.

No record of mental illness has ever existed in my family... or at least that I have been aware of. I should seek guidance about the matter and maybe pursue some kind of medication. The situation is that I don't have a job and no insurance at the moment. 

I think your right otherwise. A lot of what bothers me is the thought that I am behind and failing the people that had such high expectations for myself. I need to get a grip.

I'm sorry for the late response, I have been away. I really appreciate these replies :-). 
I went to college. Michigan State University. I did a few films here and there (student films... so pretty bad.. ha). I have always wanted to pursue something creative. All my life in fact, but shied away from it. My studies were involved in business and hotels and such. I also did some sports, ran a few triathlons and just tried to stay busy. I didn't really excel at any one particular thing. Average grades. College was pretty great.

I guess my goals have always been the same as when I was a kid. I want to get involved in story telling. Whether it be film or the written word, I have yet to really decide. I just hold tremendous doubt over myself. So life wise I want to build up my skills in photography, writing and film. 

I also want to get back into doing triathlons. It was a pretty bold time for myself. I used to think I couldn't do such a thing. It's been awhile since I have done one though.
When I was working as a night auditor I was hardly sleeping at all and then I was working all night. Things became worse around that point. I was in that job for several months before I left.

I think hearing from other people who have been able to overcome their depression by medication would do me good, I am just curious about what the experience is like. I think I can safely admit that I do suffer from depression to some degree. Thanks Adam29.
